articles.title: The ups and downs of Space X's Starship test flights
articles.summary: The BBC's Ricky Boleto looks how previous SpaceX test flights went.
articles.body:
SpaceX is planning to carry out its 14th Starship rocket test flight on Monday.

If successful, it will be the first Starship to go in orbit around the Earth and the furthest one has ever flown.

The mission is set to complete approximately six orbits around the planet over a 10-hour flight.

But as the BBC's Ricky Boleto reports, there have been many ups and downs along the way.

articles.title: "No voy a quedarme aquí, me largo, dame la radio"
articles.standfirst: Stroll y su disputa con un comisario de pista de Bakú, que le pedía que permaneciera en esa zona del circuito tras el abandono
articles.summary: Stroll y su disputa con un comisario de pista de Bakú, que le pedía que permaneciera en esa zona del circuito tras el abandono
articles.body: No es nada grave, pero sí curioso. Un aficionado captó a Lance Stroll tras abandonar en la vuelta 8 del GP de Azerbaiyán y todo el afán del canadiense, como para todos los pilotos, era volver cuanto antes a su cuartel general en la recta de meta. Estaba en la curva 15, a dos kilómetros, y uno de los comisarios de pista del circuito de Bakú. seguramente voluntario, le transmitía a Stroll lo que a él le habían dicho: cualquier piloto que abandonase en esa parte del trazado debía permanecer en esa 'isla' (seguramente todo estaba cortado o acotado durante la prueba) hasta el final de la carrera, por motivos de seguridad. La reacción de Stroll fue la lógica, después de una avería temprana, el enfado y de otro gran premio con un rendimiento más que limitado en lo mecánico por parte de Honda. Lance quería estar en el muro o ir a la ducha cuanto antes para pasar página y el bueno del comisario le pedía que no se moviese. "No voy a esperar aquí hasta el final de la sesión, me largo de aquí... dame la radio”, le pedía Stroll a su interlocutor. Las formas no fueron las más educadas, pero tampoco tenía la culpa el piloto de que no haya viales de emergencia, como sucede en Mónaco, y que los pilotos o las asistencias no puedan moverse por el perímetro de la pista. Eso también es seguridad. El comisario no tenía la culpa, pero el compañero de Alonso tampoco. Y quedaban una hora y 20 minutos para el final de la competición. "Tuvimos un problema de presión de agua, así que me indicaron que detuviera el coche. Ha sido otra semana difícil, pero somos conscientes de la situación a la que nos enfrentamos este año. No hay muchos aspectos positivos que rescatar. El objetivo es solucionar estos problemas de cara a las próximas carreras y pensando también en el horizonte de 2027", decía Stroll en el plano deportivo.

images.caption: Stroll, con el comisario de pista en Bakú. Twitter

articles.title: ‘Cohete’ sube el listón: tetracampeón del SuperCER en su campaña más dominante con Skoda
articles.standfirst: Llarena supera a Ares por la mínima tras el precipitado desenlace del Rally de Llanes
articles.summary: Llarena supera a Ares por la mínima tras el precipitado desenlace del Rally de Llanes
articles.body: José Antonio Suárez ya es con todas las de la ley el piloto referencial y ahora también el más laureado del Supercampeonato de España. El RallyRACC –donde Skoda presidirá además el cartel, y lucirá la aureola de coche oficial– asistirá dentro de unos días (16-17 de octubre) a la proclamación definitiva como tetracampeones del asturiano y su copiloto, Alberto Iglesias. Nombres propios nuevamente de un certamen donde han vuelto a subir el listón, mejorándose a sí mismos ante una competencia mayor que el año anterior. Camino de su 36º cumpleaños (el 22 de octubre), el piloto de Pravia demuestra haber alcanzado su pico de madurez deportiva. Poco a poco, ha aprendido a conjugar la valentía y velocidad que expuso desde 'guaje' con el temple y la solidez de los que adoleció en su momento, cuando intentó incansablemente hacerse un nombre en el Mundial. Estas últimas temporadas, el 'coco' de Skoda se ha ido perfeccionando cada vez más, hasta devenir ya en un auténtico especialista del Nacional: un ‘supercampeón’ de España –literal– como los Puras y Fuster con los que creció. Además de rápido y corajudo, el ‘Cohete’ actual también se ha tornado fiable y eficaz. Desde el Rally de Ourense del 2025, no ha vuelto a atizarse ningún guarrazo de aquellos tan frecuentes antes en todas sus temporadas. Ni siquiera el cambio de estructura y patrocinador que decretó en mayo alteró el rumbo del asturiano. El pinchazo de hace unos días, en el TC+ del ‘Princesa’, ha sido el único leve borrón de una temporada ejemplar, que ha liderado desde el principio. Los cinco rallies donde ha triunfado –incluido el Sierra Morena del Europeo–, el segundo puesto de Ourense y el cuarto de este fin de semana, perfilan la identidad actual de un piloto sereno y cuajado, diestro ahora sí en ganar campeonatos, que está ya marcando una época. ’Cohete’ ha contemporizado en los tramos de Llanes, a los que partió el viernes teniendo ya casi ganado un nuevo Supercampeonato, con el que desempata en la estadística a Pepe López. Los sucesivos pinchazos de Ruiloba el segundo día, por los que primero ha cedido el liderato y después se ha retirado, han zanjado definitivamente la coronación del piloto de Skoda, antes del precipitado desenlace de un rally que quedará archivado con Efrén Llarena como vencedor. 4.3 segundos separaban a falta de tramos al burgalés de Iván Ares, en pleno toma y daca cuando ha trascendido el trágico accidente por el que se ha suspendido la penúltima cita del año. La única a la que ha comparecido el subcampeón del 2022, muy combativo en todo momento, pese a llevar toda la temporada casi inactivo. Ares ha recuperado la mordiente en las carreteras de Llanes, donde Cagiao por fin ha vuelto a fluir, consiguiendo su primer 'scratch', y a la postre también su primer podio con el Lancia que acaba de estrenar. Muñiz, feliz y contento por poder volver al ruedo, ha terminado quinto. Pepe López, brioso el primer día, se ha acabado desplomando por un pinchazo, y su nuevo compañero, Arnau Bartés, ha superado las expectativas de Hyundai, cuajando un debut muy sólido con el i20N ‘pata negra’ que pilotará de nuevo en Cataluña. 1º- Efrén Llarena / Sara Fernández (Toyota GR Yaris Rally2), 55:33.9 2º- Iván Ares / Borja Rozada (Toyota GR Yaris Rally2), a 4.3 3º- Jorge Cagiao / Javier Martínez (Lancia Ypsilon Rally2 HF Integrale), a 15.0 4º- José Antonio Suárez / Alberto Iglesias (Skoda Fabia RS Rally2), a 18.0 5º- Álvaro Muñiz / Manuel Estévez (Skoda Fabia RS Rally2), a 25.2 1º- José Antonio Suárez, 240 puntos 2º- Iván Ares, 192 puntos 3º- Diego Ruiloba, 184 puntos 4º- Pepe López, 175 puntos 5º- Sergi Pérez, 146 puntos

articles.title: Kyle Larson Isn’t Frustrated by Carson Hocevar’s Fame
articles.summary: Kyle Larson says Carson Hocevar's fan following doesn't frustrate him, because fans like different. Dale Earnhardt Jr. also explained what he thinks drives H...
articles.body:
Kyle Larson says he isn't frustrated by the fan following Carson Hocevar has built, even as other NASCAR drivers push back on how Hocevar races. The reigning Cup Series champion said Hocevar's differences are what draw fans in.

Larson was asked about Hocevar during a media session at Kansas Speedway on Saturday. Hocevar's growing fan base has been a talking point since Ryan Blaney confronted him after the Bristol Night Race on Sept. 19. The two traded punches on pit road, and NASCAR chose not to penalize either driver.

Kyle Larson Says Carson Hocevar Is 'Different'

Larson and Hocevar have not had any run-ins on the track. Larson drives the No. 5 Chevrolet for Hendrick Motorsports , which has an alliance with Hocevar's Spire Motorsports team.

Asked if Hocevar's popularity surprised or frustrated him, Larson said Hocevar stands out from the rest of the field.

"No, I mean, because he's different than all of us. Acts different, talks different, dresses different. "So, I think that's refreshing for fans. And he drives more aggressive and willing to do crazier things than the rest of us probably are."

"No, I mean, because he's different than all of us. Acts different, talks different, dresses different.

"So, I think that's refreshing for fans. And he drives more aggressive and willing to do crazier things than the rest of us probably are."

Larson said he doesn't resent the attention Hocevar is getting.

"So no, I mean, it's not frustrating at all on that aspect. Like I'm not jealous of any exposure he's getting from it because he's doing a good job with it."

He added that drivers still have to be careful around the No. 77 on the track.

"He's just different and people like different. So, yeah, I think it's definitely… you have to keep your eye on him when you're on the racetrack. "But as a fan, I can see why he's likable in that aspect."

"He's just different and people like different. So, yeah, I think it's definitely… you have to keep your eye on him when you're on the racetrack.

"But as a fan, I can see why he's likable in that aspect."

Larson heads into Sunday's race at Kansas leading the Chase standings by one point over Denny Hamlin . Hocevar, 23, is eighth after finishing third at Bristol.

Dale Earnhardt Jr. offered his own read on Hocevar on the Dirty Air podcast . He said Hocevar measures his performance by how fans react.

"Oh, listen, I'm going to tell you, if you pile it all up here, he definitely is unique. If Spire wants to ask him to do some things differently, they're going to try to do that. But I feel like he goes off a fan reaction. "And if the fans are happy, and if he's getting the reaction that he wants out of that engagement with fans, then he feels like that he has done his job well."

"Oh, listen, I'm going to tell you, if you pile it all up here, he definitely is unique. If Spire wants to ask him to do some things differently, they're going to try to do that. But I feel like he goes off a fan reaction.

"And if the fans are happy, and if he's getting the reaction that he wants out of that engagement with fans, then he feels like that he has done his job well."

Earnhardt, a 26-time Cup Series winner who now works in motorsports media, said Hocevar's goal goes beyond drama.

"He wants to create… I don't think drama is the wrong word. I think he wants to create moments. And so that's what he's trying. You know, he's wanting to create moments, and the reaction the fans give him is telling his brain, 'I did my job well today.'"

He also said NASCAR's response to the Bristol fight sends Hocevar a message. Earnhardt pointed to NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell and the decision not to issue fines.

"And when NASCAR is going to come up and say, no fines, that put us up on a SportsCenter, all those things, Hocevar sees that as I made O'Donnell happy. I did my job today. "I'm doing what NASCAR prefers me to do. Right or wrong, that's what's going down."

"And when NASCAR is going to come up and say, no fines, that put us up on a SportsCenter, all those things, Hocevar sees that as I made O'Donnell happy. I did my job today.

"I'm doing what NASCAR prefers me to do. Right or wrong, that's what's going down."

Larson and Hocevar both start Sunday's Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas, the fourth of 10 races in the Chase. The race starts at 3 p.m. ET on USA Network.

articles.title: NASCAR Cup Playoffs Point Standings and Updated Schedule After 2026 Kansas Results
articles.summary: Kyle Larson used a late pass to claim his second win in four races as part of the NASCAR Cup Series Chase.
articles.body:
Kyle Larson used a late pass to claim his second win in four races as part of the NASCAR Cup Series Chase.

Larson overtook Chase Briscoe to claim the victory at the Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway.

Larson received the checkered flag in front of Austin Cindric, Denny Hamlin and Briscoe.

The victory allowed Larson to open up a 27-point advantage on Hamlin in the NASCAR playoff standings.

Larson became the first driver to win multiple playoff races this season.

The No. 5 car driver was in control for most of the race. He led 235 of the 267 laps, but he needed to come from behind to win the race.

Larson utilized a late pass on Briscoe to re-take the lead and finish off his dominant day at Kansas.

Briscoe was the only other driver to lead more than 10 laps on Sunday. He tried to hold on to first, but Larson was too much for him to hold off.

Briscoe eventually dropped back to fourth place after Cindric and Hamlin passed him over the final few laps.

Larson now owns a 27-point advantage over Hamlin, the regular-season points champion, in the playoff points standings.

Christopher Bell in third place is the only other driver within 50 points of Larson. Joey Logano, Ryan Blaney and Ty Gibbs are within 100 points of the No. 5 driver.

A trip to Las Vegas is up next for the Cup Series. Hamlin was the spring winner at Las Vegas earlier this season.

Larson did lead 62 laps of the spring Vegas race, so he will be a threat to win once again in his attempt to balloon the playoff lead with six races to go.

articles.title: Antonelli sí vio al 'misil' Colapinto y lo evitó sobre la marcha
articles.standfirst: Observó la blocada del argentino por delante, frenó y cambió su trayectoria para esquivar el posible choque
articles.summary: Observó la blocada del argentino por delante, frenó y cambió su trayectoria para esquivar el posible choque
articles.body: KImi Antonelli y la forma en la que evitó el choque que se produjo entre los Alpine (y un posible abandono a falta de 15 vueltas), era una de las imágenes que se hicieron virales tras acabar quinto y remontar 11 puestos en Azerbaiyán. Hay quien sostiene que fue pura suerte o casualidad, pero viendo la imagen de la cámara de su coche parece que hubo mucho de anticipación y talento. Kimi reconoce que no iba a por la remontada como en Monza. "Estaba conduciendo un poco como mi abuela, en modo de ahorro de daños. No corrí ningún riesgo. Antes de actuar, me aseguré de que podía hacerlo. En definitiva, es uno de esos días en los que hay que estar contento con el quinto puesto", confesaba mostrando un criterio bien elegido. "Sí, sin duda, si hubiera tenido el mismo ritmo que en Monza o carreras anteriores habría sido diferente. Habría sido un ataque total. Pero me di cuenta muy pronto de que, en primer lugar, era mucho más difícil adelantar con una fila de coches en modo de adelantamiento. Y además no tenía el mismo ritmo que antes, así que mi mentalidad cambió muy rápidamente", explicaba sobre lo que sintió y lo que decidió. "Además, al ver a tanta gente cometiendo errores, me contuve un poco porque simplemente quería aprovecharme de los errores de los demás y seguir adelante", concedía sobre un modo de pilotar para llegar a meta, lo que se antoja como la mejor decisión posible. Franco Colapinto llegó en la resalida de la vuelta 36 como un misil, pero Kimi pudo verlo por delante de su coche y tomar contramedidas. "Vi que el Alpine bloqueaba y frené inmediatamente. Me estaba preparando para hacer una curva cerrada, pero entonces no vi a Ollie (Bearman) venir tan rápido por dentro...", relataba Antonelli no salió indemne del embudo. "Tuve que frenar bruscamente, porque todavía estaba muy cerca del Alpine cuando volví a girar, pero el suelo quedó muy dañado. Todo el lado izquierdo quedó destrozado con el impacto, y después de eso, el coche era muy difícil de conducir", dice sobre un impacto con el Haas del británico que no se vio. "Obviamente, tuve suerte de salir ileso. No tuve tanta suerte de salir con daños severos, pero en general, no pasó nada grave", cerraba. Fue un movimiento de supervivencia que logró su propósito. El quinto final fue un gran resultado para él.

images.caption: Antonelli frenó para evitar a los Alpine y pasar de largo por detrás. F1TV

articles.title: Crecen los rumores sobre un cambio de jefatura en Ferrari... Y hay una sombra de fondo
articles.standfirst: Fred Vasseur parece que saldrá al final de la temporada, pero hay quien señala ya que podría salir antes de que acabe 2026
articles.summary: Fred Vasseur parece que saldrá al final de la temporada, pero hay quien señala ya que podría salir antes de que acabe 2026
articles.body: El decreciente rendimiento en las últimas citas tras el verano, justo cuando llegaron las mejoras para el SF-26, tanto en el motor como en la aerodinámica, están causando una ola de intenso ruido en los medios italianos sobre el futuro inmediato de Ferrari. Fred Vasseur está en el disparadero y se ha filtrado que el presidente de la marca, John Elkann habría sondeado en las últimas horas a Antonio Coletta, director del equipo del WEC para hacerse con las riendas de la histórica escudería. No es probable que sea en medio de este triplete de carreras encadenadas, pero es una opción que va cobrando fuerza. En caso de que Coletta no aceptara, se habla incluso de Jerome D'Ambrosio, actual segundo de Vasseur, como la persona que podría realizar una transición hasta el final de la tempòrada. Es cierto que siempre hay mucho estruendo en torno a Ferrari, con una exigencia máxima, pero la imagen en Bakú de sus dos pilotos, Hamilton y Leclerc, quienes no pudieron oponer nada contra los Red Bull de Verstappen y Hadjar, ha hecho mucho dañó en las últimas horas. Y por detrás de las soluciones de la casa se cierne la alargada sombra de Christian Horner, ya habilitado para volver a la F1 tras su periodo de exclusión obligatoria al salir de Red Bull en agosto de 2025. El británico atesora ocho Mundiales de pilotos con Vettel y Verstappen y en los principales medios italianos no se le descarta como un posible nuevo director de equipo, sobre todo a partir de 2027. Vesseur fue renovado en junio de 2025 con Ferrari (se supone que por dos años), ya entre una intensa marejada por la falta de resultados tras la llegada de Lewis Hamilton. El mes de junio fue el de un despertar de la Scuderia, con el triunfo de Lewis en Barcelona y el de Leclerc en Silverstone, pero a partir de ese momento el desplome ha sido tan largo como vertical para los monoplazas rojos. Hamilton es tercero el el campeonato del mundo, a 103 puntos del italiano Antonelli, algo que también pesa en el ferrarismo, y Leclerc es cuarto a 132 puntos de Kimi. Los lunes son especialmente difíciles en Maranello en estas circunstancias.

articles.title: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says Christian Horner 'looking for a job' adding to 'frustrating' speculation around F1 team
articles.summary: Ex-Red Bull chief Christian Horner said Ferrari would be the only team he would consider coming back to F1 for without an ownership stake; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
articles.body:
Vasseur, who joined Ferrari as team principal from Sauber in 2023, has an overseen their return to race-winning ways this year after a poor 2025 but their world championship challenge to Mercedes has faded in recent months amid a five-race run without a podium finish.

In an interview with The Times published last week, former Red Bull team principal Horner said Ferrari were the only team he would consider returning to the pit-wall for without the ownership stake that he has been prioritising for any comeback to the sport.

Asked after Sunday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, in which his drivers finished fourth and sixth, whether the external noise around him and the team recently was affecting them, Vasseur conceded it was frustrating.

"We are not working in perfect serenity," said Vasseur.

"For me, first, but for everybody in the team, for the media, for the 50 per cent of the questions about this. I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation.

"We are fighting for P2 in the championship. At the end of the day, we are all speaking a lot about this, and even for the guys in the garage to discuss about this, it's not the best discussion that we can have.

"But it is what it is, it's not in my hands."

Referencing his former Red Bull counterpart, Vasseur added: "Mr Horner is looking for a job. Everybody knows, everywhere.

"What can I do? I just try to do my best to push the team, to ask the team to be motivated, focus on what is better today, and not to spend time with gossips.

"In each interview, it will be 25 times a day."

Vasseur signed a multi-year contract extension last year and said there was no doubt about his commitment to the role as he bids to lead F1's most-famous team back to world title-winning ways for the first time since 2008.

"For sure. The sport is my life, it's my business," said the 58-year-old Vasseur. "I'm trying to do my best. For sure, I'm there to do my job. I have the best job in the world.

"It is like it is. We still have seven races to go and we will push to the last corner."

Lewis Hamilton credited the presence of Vasseur, who he worked with in junior series, as a central reason for him joining Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025. The seven-time world champion replied "yes" when asked by Sky Sports F1 after the Baku race whether the team remained on a good path forward with Vasseur at the helm.

Villeneuve: Horner someone you must have under consideration

Even before he was sacked by Red Bull in July 2025, Horner had been intermittently linked with Ferrari over the years owing to the success which saw the Briton lead their rivals to eight drivers' and six constructors' world titles.

Sky Sports F1 pundit Jacques Villeneuve believes Horner's availability has to be a consideration for a team.

"Christian Horner is someone you have to take seriously and under consideration because he built up the winning Red Bull team," the 1997 world champion told Sky Sports News in Baku.

"He has a lot of very good and positive baggage, full of successes so you have to take that into consideration.

"I wouldn't say it's scary for who is in place, but you need to be on your toes."

Vasseur became Ferrari's fifth team principal in nine years when he was hired from the start of the 2023 season, with the current campaign his fourth in charge.

Villeneuve added: "Ferrari is not an easy place to be. We have seen so many changes - two or three years, next one, because the results don't come.

"So you are always on an ejectable seat and you have to be careful."

articles.body:
3.15 Brighton - Danehill Star chases a hat-trick

Danehill Star chases a hat-trick in the Bet £20 Get £40 in Free Bets at matchbook.com Handicap .

The Tony Carroll-trained gelding has been in the form of his life, winning on his last two starts. The first came over course and distance by half a length, before he bolted up by over five lengths at Bath.

The handicapper has not missed him, as he has been raised ten pounds since these wins, but the manner in which he won at Bath suggests that he holds strong claims in rounding off a hat-trick of wins.

Newfangled perhaps poses the biggest threat having won this race last season off just a one-pound lower mark. He has hit form at the right time, finishing a creditable third at Windsor last time out.

Course-specialist Dion Baker has found it tough from a mark of 73, a rise of 36 pounds since beginning his winning run at the track in late May. He holds a chance, having fallen two pounds in the handicap, and On The Inlet could be competitive if he can resume his early-season progression back down in class.

2.25 Newton Abbot - Dovecote fourth Matiwo returns

Dovecote fourth Matiwo returns in the Jodie Standing's Point-To-Point Recruits Novices' Hurdle .

Matiwo looked a promising juvenile hurdler last season having won a decent Newbury novice in taking fashion before finishing a brilliant fourth in the Grade Two Dovecote Hurdle where he travelled like one of the best in the race. That day he beat some exciting types including subsequent Grade One Top Novices' Hurdle winner, Storming George.

His current form and unexposed profile puts him well above his opposition and he should prove very tough to beat on seasonal reappearance.

Ride Like A Girl looked promising after wind surgery when winning in May but has not progressed since. If coming on for his last run following a short break, he could be competitive with experience and fitness onside.

Scott's Legacy would pose the chief threat if taking to obstacles on hurdle debut, having won impressively in a good bumper at Southwell in March.

Pappano contains a lot of ability having been rated 96 on the flat and contested this year's Triumph hurdle for Willie Mullins. He has not shaped with much promise on two hurdling starts and raced too keenly last time out, and now has plenty to prove.

4.55 Wolverhampton - Record-breaking 1-33 loser Najidi Storm faces Wootz

Record-breaking 1-33 loser Najidi Storm faces exciting Wootz in the Download the At the Races App Novice Stakes .

Najidi Storm was mightily impressive on debut when scoring with by half a length with a taking turn of foot. That novice has worked out well with two next-time-out winners, including the subsequent Cambridgeshire fourth, Gavriel. He then seemed to dislike heavy conditions at Goodwood when becoming the shortest-priced loser in British racing history at 1-33.

He is brother to St Leger winner Logician, and half-brother to smart performer Okeechobee, so contains plenty of scope for further improvement.

Opposition is stiff with the exciting Wootz sure to prove a stern rival.

articles.title: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto over ban comments after Azerbaijan Grand Prix
articles.summary: World champion Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for saying the Argentine should be banned for causing an accident at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto for saying the Argentine should be banned for causing an accident at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto locked up at the restart after a safety-car period and slid into Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who then hit McLaren driver Norris, in an incident which resulted in all three retiring from the race.

Colapinto said he was "sorry" for his "big mistake" but Norris, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, said: "Give him a ban. It's quite simple."

In a message on Instagram, world champion Norris said he was sorry for his comments on Saturday.

"Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race," he said.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said.

"I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me.

"I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

Colapinto was given a 10-second penalty during the race, but as he was already retired this has been converted into a five-place grid drop, which he will serve at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia this weekend.

images.caption: Image caption, Franco Colapinto's lock-up in Turn One took out his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly as well as McLaren's Lando Norris

articles.title: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto for critical comments made about Alpine driver following Azerbaijan GP crash
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto caused a collision with his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris that took all three of them out of the Azerbaijan GP; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix
articles.body:
Colapinto triggered the accident during a Safety Car restart in Baku when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of his Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident in Saturday's race, Norris said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1" and called for such incidents to result in one-race bans for the initiator.

Colapinto apologised to both Gasly and Norris during his post-race interviews, but the Argentine driver was handed a five-place grid penalty for this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

On Monday morning, Norris posted on Instagram: "Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said.

"I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me.

"I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

The incident and Norris' initial criticism caused a social media furore, with users criticising Colapinto for his driving, and the Brit for his comments.

The fallout led to Alpine releasing a statement on Sunday condemning the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in F1 that had followed the incident.

It's not the first time Alpine have spoken out against social media abuse this season, with the online conduct of Colapinto's fans having previously come under scrutiny.

FIA stewards and Alpine staff were targeted when Colapinto received a drive-through penalty for overtaking under a double yellow flag in Zandvoort.

Gasly was also abused after briefly refusing to let Colapinto past him during the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid earlier this month. The Frenchman revealed the threats targeted his family too.

Colapinto said after the Madrid fallout that it's "never nice to get" social media abuse, but insisted that it's "not just my fans" who are guilty of it.

Alpine appeared to attempt to avoid antagonising Colapinto's fans in their latest statement by insisting their statement wasn't "aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver".

The statement said: "As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula 1 community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned."

articles.title: Norris reconoce que se pasó con Colapinto
articles.standfirst: El piloto de McLaren ofrece una disculpa formal a Colapinto por redes sociales
articles.summary: El piloto de McLaren ofrece una disculpa formal a Colapinto por redes sociales
articles.body: El Mundial de F1 está viviendo unos días un tanto convulsos a raíz del incidente entre Franco Colapinto, Pierre Gasly y Lando Norris durante la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. El fallo del piloto argentino en la primera resalida al pasarse de frenada en la recta y llevarse por medio a su compañero de equipo, Pierre Gasly, y al Campeón del Mundo 2025, Lando Norris, ha desencadenado un polvorín mediático opacando, en gran medida, la victoria de Russell y su posible reenganche en el Mundial. Dicha acción, cuyas consecuencias pudieron ser extremadamente graves, han conllevado a la imposición por parte de la FIA de una sanción de cinco posiciones en parrilla al piloto argentino, la cual deberá cumplir este mismo fin de semana en Sepang. A parte de Gasly, Norris salió bastante damnificado de tal embrollo. El inglés, a quien ya de por sí no le estaba yendo bien el fin de semana, acabó fuera de carrera tras ser embestido por Gasly, a consecuencia del toque con Colapinto. Norris, quien veía factible al menos un 7º u 8º puesto, cargó duramente contra el argentino, con una frase que retumbó y se hizo viral en cuestión de minutos: "Hay pilotos que no deberían estar en la F1", sentenció Lando ante tal precipitado final de carrera y la falta de disculpas por parte del argentino hacia él, "me he disculpado con Pierre y con el equipo", comentó Colapinto en el parque cerrado tras la carrera. Dichas palabras del británico suscitaron a los fans de la F1, lanzándose contra ambos pilotos y provocando una oleada de críticas. 'Chocapinto' o 'Blando Norris' volvieron a leerse entre los comentarios de los vídeos e imágenes que mostraban las secuencias del accidente, generando un polvorín de 'hate' prácticamente inaguantable. Ante tal nivel de odio en las redes sociales, muchos han sido los que han salido en defensa del piloto de Alpine, a quien se le vio claramente afligido y arrepentido tras el incidente que le costó su carrera, la de su compañero de equipo y la de Norris. El 'Kun' Agüero ha sido, sin lugar a duda, la más sonada, saliendo en defensa de su compatriota y, levantando de tal manera, 'hate' hacia el inglés. Todo este periplo que se ha montado ha llegado hasta un extremo en el que Lando Norris ha publicado en sus redes sociales una disculpa formal hacia Franco Colapinto. "Un fin de semana duro en general en Bakú y, por supuesto, un final de carrera decepcionante y anticipado. Después de la carrera, le envié un mensaje a Franco pidiéndole disculpas por los comentarios que hice, que simplemente no debería haber dicho. Sé que las emociones estaban a flor de piel, pero eso no es una excusa, fue un error por mi parte. He cometido errores en mi carrera y seguiré cometiéndolos, y esta es una gran parte de las carreras y de luchar al limite. Franco y yo tenemos una buena relación, seguimos siendo buenos amigos y ambos estamos deseando volver a competir juntos este fin de semana". De esta manera, el piloto de McLaren busca zanjar la polémica y centrarse en el próximo Gran Premio tratando de mejorar, además, aspectos de su monoplaza con los que no llegó a sentirse del todo a gusto en Bakú.

images.caption: Lando Norris durante el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Darko Bendic.
La disculpa de Lando Norris a través de su cuenta de Instagram.

articles.title: La cruda realidad de los dos españoles de aquí a final de año... con matices
articles.standfirst: Alonso espera a Singapur como carrera marcada y Sainz quiere ver en Sepang si la mejora de Williams es real o sólo puntual por el trazado
articles.summary: Alonso espera a Singapur como carrera marcada y Sainz quiere ver en Sepang si la mejora de Williams es real o sólo puntual por el trazado
articles.body: La de Bakú fue una carrera de alivio para Carlos Sainz y Williams, al poder materializar un punto el madrileño. Era importante certificar el salto de rendimiento, que les ha metido de nuevo en la lucha de la zona media, aunque hay ciertas cautelas por parte de Carlos. Sepang, este mismo fin de semana, es una pista con muchas curvas de radio amplio puede ser un escenario de nuevo complicado para el FW48, aunque un buen banco de pruebas para ver la realidad de ese chasis aligerado, que iba acompañado de suelo, pontones difusor y retoques en la suspensión delantera. Sainz está expectante por lo que puede pasar en el GP de Bahréin, que se aplazó en abril por la guerra y que encuentra en Sepang un viejo conocido para el '55'. De hecho, fue el circuito donde debutó en la Fórmula BMW en 2010, con 15 años y donde ganó una carrera con Daniil Kvyat como compañero de equipo. Ese conocimiento de una pista exigente con el motor y la eficiencia aerodinámica a partes iguales, no es considerado por Carlos como una gran ventaja respecto al resto de la parrilla. "Creo que no es ventaja ya hoy en día conocerlo y más que nada porque con tres libres como tenemos los pilotos de Fórmula 1 nos espabilamos rápido", bromeaba en ESPN. "Pero es un circuito divertido que yo creo que además a nosotros como equipo nos va a dejar evaluar mejor el paquete que hemos traído", confesaba. La realidad se sabrá allí, aunque Sainz se marchaba de Azerbaiyán con una predicción un tanto pesimista. "Será difícil que volvamos a puntuar de aquí al final", lanzaba como vaticinio. Por lo menos, en un lugar en el que los neumáticos no entraban en calor, Carlos descubrió una forma de alcanzar la temperatura óptima en la Q3 del pasado viernes. Y eso era algo que era un talón de Aquiles en los últimos años para todos los Williams. Puede que sea un punto de partida para mejorar en las parrillas de salida. Dejando a un lado la discusión de si había un fallo en el motor en la carrera, que Honda niega, su realidad se ha revelado con toda crudeza en Monza, Madrid y Bakú, con tres resultados terribles en distancia respecto a los rivales y en cuanto a fiabilidad. Stroll no ha terminado ninguna carrera con la spec nueva que llegó en Holanda la última semana de agosto y Alonso puntuó con el noveno allí, pero luego la falta de potencia le ha condenado luego. "La realidad es la que es", repite al asturiano, que sabe que tiene 60 CV menos que los más potentes de la parrilla, algo insalvable. En Sepang, una de sus pistas favoritas, donde logró su primera pole en 2023 por delante del ferrari de Schumacher, pese a estar con 39 grados de fiebre, podrá maquillar en la zona virada, pues el Aston no es un mal coche en curva media, pero en las dos rectas finales, de casi un kilómetro, todo irá para abajo como sucedía en el tramo final de Bakú. Singapur, una semana más tarde y Brasil, ya en noviembre, parecen los trazados más favorables para Alonso en lo que resta del año. La clave es si en Honda podrán reconducir la situación para 2027, porque el salto la spec 2 de 2026 se ha confirmado como pírrico o prácticamente inapreciable.

One vendor at Martinsville Speedway got more of a show than they were expecting at Saturday's ValleyStar Credit Union 300.

articles.title: Rising NASCAR star jumped, attacked & beaten at America's most famous hot dog shack
articles.summary: NASCAR driver Corey Heim ate punches near the famous Martinsville hot dog stand after going airborne over Treyten Lapcevich's hood in a wild wreck.
articles.body: Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists. I tell you what, if NASCAR's big idea to stay relevant during the fall is to just start throwing punches every weekend ... I think I'm in. It's not the worst idea in the world. Frankly, it just might work. That's right. Another weekend, another viral fight in the racing world. This one didn't take place during a Cup race, but it did involve a NASCAR driver. Heck, it involved a NASCAR winner! NASCAR DRIVER SAYS QUIET PART OUT LOUD ABOUT SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM, THE WNBA LOOKS EVEN WORSE & CAR GOES AIRBORNE! Wait till you see this beatdown poor Corey Heim took at Martinsville Saturday night. Just a brutal attack. And right in front of a hot dog stand, no less! Disgusting stuff. You'll see. As for the NASCAR Cup Series ... Kyle Larson won at Kansas in a race that featured a handful of green flag passes for the lead, which is always a sign of a great race! At least it was a halfway decent finish. We've also got more fallout from Carson Hocevar giving Ryan Blaney a black eye last weekend at Bristol, but that rivalry is pretty much dead on arrival, folks. Those two spent all week basically dating each other through the media. So much for that storyline. The good news? Carson's already been wrecked again! I'm not sure this one was intentional, though. You'll see. Four tires, enough fuel to get us through the final full month of the 2026 season, and maybe a free Martinsville hot dog for poor Corey Heim ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'Grown Men Acting Like a Bunch Of Weiners' edition — is LIVE! Corey Heim attacked by a hot dog stand So, this is the wreck that everyone and their mother is talking about from this past weekend. Corey Heim — who won Cup races at San Diego and Indy this season — was racing in a late model event in Martinsville. He battled hard over the final few laps as folks tend to do at Martinsville, and got into Treyten Lapcevich after the checkered flag. And by "got into," I mean ... well, he went up the track, spun Lapcevich, and promptly went airborne over his hood. Lordy. What a wreck! You don't see that very often in Martinsville. But, this is also a late model race. These ain't your modern day NASCAR stock cars. They're actually way better, but that's a story for another time. Anyway, this was a big race. A big event. The ValleyStar Credit Union 300 is often described as the Daytona 500 for these drivers. It's been around for over five decades. It's a big deal. Emotions were running HOT after this race, especially after Heim parked himself on Lapcevich's hood. One thing led to another, and, as Corey was trying to cool off with a nice, Martinsville hot dog ... he started eating helmets and fists: Corey Heim eats a couple punches, but why? Goodness gracious. What a fight! Well, it wasn't really a fight. Like last weekend's "fight" between Hocevar and Blaney, this "fight" was really just one person(s) beating the hell out of another. It was pretty lopsided. Corey just ate punch after punch. He had a helmet, and didn't even use it! Again, all of this right in front of the famous Martinsville hot dog shack. Disgusting. PS: Ever had a Martinsville hot dog? Amazing. No, they're not regular hot dogs. The first time I saw one, I was floored. They're these tiny, little, bright red hot dogs and buddy, they will change your life. And I'm not even a big hot dog guy. Anyway, back to Corey ... "Solid effort, but at least make it count next time," Heim said via his X account on Saturday, with an accompanying picture of him looking completely normal. Well done, Corey. Solid response. As for the fight ... Heim was clearly in the wrong ... on the track. I don't know exactly what he was doing after the checkered flag, but it's tough to pin any of that on Treyten Lapcevich. That being said, it's a pretty embarrassing look for the Chad Bryant Racing team — including Chad Bryant himself — to just gang up on a kid and start beating the piss out of him when he clearly has no intention of fighting back. Now, why didn't he fight back, you might ask? I would assume because A) he's got a full-time Cup ride with 23XI lined up for next season, and B) he was wearing a 23XI firesuit. Would Michael Jordan really care that much if one of his future drivers defended himself? I doubt it. He'd probably prefer it. But, Corey wasn't gonna take that chance. That's my guess. Dale Earnhardt Jr ... thoughts on this? Larson, Blaney & Carson, oh my! "The thing of it is, those are some damn good hotdogs," Junior tweeted out Saturday night. Couldn't agree more, brother! It's important to keep things in perspective. Thanks, Dale. OK, let's put the pedal to the floor and kick this thing into high gear on this final Monday of September. First up? We DID have a NASCAR Cup Series race this weekend, and it was the Kyle Larson show. Larson led 235 of the 267 laps, scored 76 points on the day, and is now your Chase leader with six races to go. Yeah, Chase Briscoe briefly took the lead late in the race, but it was never going to hold up. Larson was, by far, the most dominant car yesterday. Barring a freak wreck, he was always going to win — mainly because it's nearly impossible to pass in these cars. Speaking of wrecks ... let's go ahead and check in on Carson Hocevar! Eh. I don't know. The announcers try to make it sound like Brad Keselowski did it on purpose, but I don't see that. Yes, Brad is going to wreck Carson this season after what happened a few weeks ago. It's gonna happen. He said as much. But not like that. NASCAR'S MOST POPULAR DRIVER HAS A TIKTOK GIRLFRIEND THAT'S CAUSING A STIR, AND HE DOESN'T CARE Brad Keselowski is a vet. He's not gonna wreck someone intentionally and put others cars in peril. That took out a ton of drivers. It wasn't payback. It was Brad getting Carson loose right in the middle of the pack on a restart. Bad recipe. But not a nefarious one. Finally ... while we're talking about Carson Hocevar ... it appears last weekend's fight with Ryan Blaney was a one-off, because these two fellas couldn't have been nicer to each other this week. Frankly, it was a bit much: Blaney admitting defeat — "I went over there and I got my a– kicked" — and Hocevar in turn talking about how much of a "stand-up guy" Blaney is doesn't exactly scream RIVALRY! So, yeah, this one is dead, folks. Blaney went on Denny Hamlin's podcast and talked about eating "two-piece," and Hocevar spent 10 minutes in the media center this weekend talking about how much he respected him. We can go ahead and put a bow on this one. It was fun while it lasted, though! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. Let's have a big week and end September with a bang. Here's Carson's TikTok girlfriend, Tabitha Swatosh, sending the HATERS a postcard from Italy on the way out. See y'all at Vegas.

articles.title: Leclerc: "No podemos engañarnos a nosotros mismos"
articles.standfirst: Asegura que Ferrari debe asumir la realidad. Los rivales han mejorado su chasis el motor ADUO 2 no les ha dado todo lo que esperaban
articles.summary: Asegura que Ferrari debe asumir la realidad. Los rivales han mejorado su chasis el motor ADUO 2 no les ha dado todo lo que esperaban
articles.body: Ferrari está viviendo los momentos más complicados del año, sin nadie en el podio en las tres últimas citas y perdiendo posiciones en carrera con rivales a los que dominaban en el inicio del curso. “No debemos engañarnos: McLaren y Red Bull han dado un gran paso adelante. Creo que Mercedes también está dando pasos adelante en cuanto a velocidad en las curvas", afirmaba el monegasco en 'Sky Sports' sobre el progreso de los demás y el estancamiento del SF-26. “Por lo tanto, no creo que tengamos el mejor chasis, como el que teníamos al principio de la temporada", sentenciaba. "Y esto es algo en lo que tenemos que trabajar y volver a un nivel mejor en ese aspecto”. La actualización del motor ADUO2 de Ferrari, presentada en Monza, no ha reducido su déficit de potencia con respecto a equipos como Mercedes y Red Bull. Se decía que tenía 20 CV extra, pero no se han notado en calificación, pero sobre todo en carrera. “Sí, creo que le faltaba velocidad en línea recta, pero no solo eso. El ritmo puro simplemente no estaba a la altura en comparación con un Red Bull, en comparación con un Mercedes”, añadía tras la carrera de Bakú.. “El McLaren estuvo bien en algunos momentos, pero tuvimos una mala salida, lo que lamentablemente condicionó toda la carrera posterior. Así que, una lástima. Tenía esperanzas de quedar segundo, pero, siendo realistas, sabíamos que sería una carrera difícil”, finalizaba. Ferrari alcanza este año su temporada 20ª (19 años) desde que consiguió su último título de pilotos en 2007 con Raikkonen y eso se acerca ya a la peor racha de su historia, cuando pasaron 21 años desde el Mundial de Jody Schekter en 1979 al primero de Michael Schumacher en 2000.
